usda_pct_limited_access_low_income.long_name: Low-Income and Low Food-Access Population (USDA Food Environment Atlas)
usda_pct_limited_access_low_income.short_description: Share of county population that is low-income and lives more than 1 mile (urban) or 10 miles (rural) from a grocery store.
usda_pct_limited_access_low_income.long_description: Percentage of the county population that is both low-income (at or below 200% of the federal poverty line) and has limited access to a grocery store, from the USDA Economic Research Service's Food Environment Atlas (variable PCT_LACCESS_LOWI19). This is USDA's own county-level aggregation of tract-level data from the separate Food Access Research Atlas. The underlying low-access variables were last updated for 2019 and have not been refreshed since, despite newer overall Atlas releases. Three Alaska boroughs (Chugach 02063, Copper River 02066, Valdez-Cordova 02261) are NA in the source due to a FIPS reorganization. Intended as the direct-source input behind PopHIVE/us-rates' chr_limited_access_to_healthy_foods measure -- County Health Rankings & Roadmaps is itself still using this same 2019 vintage.
usda_pct_limited_access_low_income.statement: In {location}, {value} of the population is low-income with limited access to healthy food.

usda_fea.name: Food Environment Atlas
usda_fea.organization: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Economic Research Service
usda_fea.description: The Food Environment Atlas assembles county-level statistics on food environment indicators, including store/restaurant availability, food and nutrition assistance programs, food insecurity, and food access. Its ACCESS sheet includes USDA's own county-level aggregation of the tract-level Food Access Research Atlas, including the percent of the population that is low-income and has limited access to a grocery store. Used here as the direct source for county-level limited healthy food access.
usda_fea.restrictions: Public domain. USDA data are generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
